title: Symphony No. 6 in F major, “Pastoral”
hook: A day in the country, from the first breath of air to the thanksgiving after a storm.

painting.title: Heroic Landscape with Rainbow
painting.collection: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
painting.pairingNote: A herdsman pipes to his goats while the clouds part and a rainbow spans the valley; an Austrian contemporary of Beethoven paints the calm after the storm.

facts: Beethoven loved the countryside and spent much of his time walking in it; he often left Vienna to work in the country. His first sketches for this symphony date from 1802, and he finished it in 1808, alongside the Fifth.
Both symphonies were first heard in the same concert, on 22 December 1808 at the Theater an der Wien: a long, under-rehearsed programme of about four hours.

Each movement has a title by Beethoven, from “Awakening of cheerful feelings on arriving in the country” to “Shepherd’s song”. But he insisted in the programme of the first performance that the symphony was “more the expression of feeling than painting”.
It has five movements instead of the usual four, and the last three run together without a pause: a village dance is cut short by a storm, and the storm clears into a song of thanks.
bigPicture.inOneLine: arriving in the country (I), a brook with birdsong (II), a village dance (III), a thunderstorm (IV), a shepherds’ hymn of thanks (V).

movements.heading: Awakening of cheerful feelings on arriving in the country
movements.title: Awakening of cheerful feelings on arriving in the country
movements.summary: No drama: a low, open drone and a short, folk-like tune, like stepping out into fresh air. Beethoven builds whole passages by repeating one small figure over and over, the way a field or a hedgerow repeats a pattern. It is a [[sonata-form|sonata form]], but its mood barely changes.

mainIdeas.name: The drone
mainIdeas.description: a low, open chord held by violas and cellos, like a bagpipe.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 1
mainIdeas.description: a short tune in the violins; its little second bar is the figure Beethoven repeats again and again.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 2
mainIdeas.description: a gentle falling melody over a rocking accompaniment in the cellos.

stops.hear: Violas and cellos hold a low, open chord; above it the violins play a short, simple tune and stop on a long held note
stops.happening: The opening: a drone, and the first breath of country air

stops.hear: A tiny figure from the tune is repeated over and over, swelling each time
stops.happening: A whole passage built from one small cell

stops.hear: A gentle, falling melody in the violins over rocking cellos
The opening returns
The little figure from the tune is played dozens of times in a row while the harmony underneath shifts, like light moving over a landscape
The opening tune returns in the violins, with a new rippling accompaniment
The tune is passed between clarinet, bassoon and strings, more and more softly

stops.label: Near the end
stops.hear: A last, quiet statement of the tune; the movement closes gently

notice: In the development, count how many times the same one-bar figure returns. The harmony changes; the figure does not.

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: Böhm’s tempos are unhurried throughout. His *Scene by the brook* lasts almost 14 minutes; Karajan’s 1977 recording, recommended above, takes about eleven and a half. On the Spotify album the symphony is tracks 1–5, followed by Schubert’s Symphony No. 5.

movements.heading: Scene by the brook
movements.title: Scene by the brook
movements.summary: A slow, murmuring movement. The strings make the sound of running water while the violins sing a long, lazy melody above it. Near the end the music stops for three birds, which Beethoven names in the score.

mainIdeas.name: The brook
mainIdeas.description: a soft, rocking figure in the lower strings, led by two [[muted|muted]] solo cellos.

mainIdeas.name: The melody
mainIdeas.description: a slow, gentle tune in the first violins, floating over the water.

stops.hear: A soft, rocking murmur in the lower strings; above it the first violins sing a slow, gentle melody
stops.happening: The brook. Two muted solo cellos play the flowing figure

stops.hear: A new, broader melody in the woodwinds and violins, over the same murmur
The music drifts into shadowy, unexpected keys; the murmur never stops
The opening melody returns in the home key
Everything pauses for three solo birds: the flute trills like a nightingale, the oboe repeats a short call like a quail, two clarinets sing “cuck-oo”
stops.happening: Beethoven wrote the names of the birds into the score

stops.label: Last 40 seconds
stops.hear: The birds call once more; the brook closes with two quiet chords

notice: Listen under the melody. The murmuring water runs through almost the entire movement.
In the birdsong, try to tell the three birds apart: one trills, one repeats a quick three-note call, one sings two falling notes.

movements.heading: Merry gathering of country people
movements.title: Merry gathering of country people
movements.summary: A village dance. A light tune in the strings is answered by the whole orchestra; then a little band strikes up, with an oboe a fraction off the beat and a bassoon that seems to know only three notes. A heavy, stamping dance follows. Everything is played twice, and then the dance speeds up until it is cut off by the storm.

mainIdeas.name: The dance
mainIdeas.description: a quick tune in three, soft in the strings and loud in reply.

mainIdeas.name: The village band
mainIdeas.description: a jaunty oboe tune over a bassoon playing just a few notes.

mainIdeas.name: The stamping dance
mainIdeas.description: a rough, heavy dance in two.

stops.hear: A light, quick tune in the strings, answered loudly by the whole orchestra
stops.happening: The country dance, in F major

stops.hear: An oboe plays a jaunty tune that seems to come in slightly late; a bassoon adds a few notes underneath; then clarinet and horn take the tune
The beat changes to a heavy, stamping two; loud and rough
The whole sequence starts again: the light dance, the band, the stamping
stops.happening: Beethoven repeats the dance and its trio

stops.hear: The first dance returns and gets faster and faster

stops.label: Near the end
stops.hear: The whirling dance breaks off on a held note
stops.happening: The storm is coming. The next movement follows without a pause ([[attacca|attacca]])

notice: Listen to the bassoon under the oboe’s tune. It plays only a handful of notes, at the bottom of each phrase, like a village player who knows his three notes and sticks to them.

movements.heading: Thunderstorm
movements.title: Thunderstorm
movements.summary: The shortest movement and the loudest. A distant rumble, the first drops of rain, and then the storm breaks with full force. The timpani, silent until now, are the thunder; a piccolo shrieks like lightning. Then the storm moves away, and the music opens straight into the finale.

mainIdeas.name: The rumble
mainIdeas.description: a low, quiet tremble in cellos and basses.

mainIdeas.name: The storm
mainIdeas.description: rushing strings, timpani thunder, piccolo lightning, and trombones at the height.

stops.hear: A distant rumble in cellos and basses; short, nervous notes in the second violins, like the first drops of rain
stops.happening: The storm approaches, in F minor

stops.hear: The full orchestra crashes in; the timpani thunder; the strings rush up and down
stops.happening: The storm breaks. The timpani play for the first time in the symphony

stops.hear: A high, piercing piccolo above the orchestra
stops.happening: Lightning. The piccolo plays only in this movement

stops.hear: Trombones join; the loudest passage of the whole symphony
The thunder grows fainter and further away; the rain eases

stops.label: Last 30 seconds
stops.hear: An oboe plays a calm, hymn-like phrase; then a single flute climbs slowly up a scale
stops.happening: The sky clears. The flute’s rising scale is often heard as a rainbow; the finale follows without a break

notice: The timpani and piccolo have waited three movements for this. Notice how much bigger the storm sounds because of it.

movements.heading: Shepherd's song: cheerful and thankful feelings after the storm
movements.title: Shepherd's song: cheerful and thankful feelings after the storm
movements.summary: After the storm, a shepherd’s call on the clarinet and the horn, and then a broad, swaying hymn of thanks in the violins. The tune returns again and again, each time more richly dressed, rises to a glowing climax and ends in a hushed, prayer-like [[coda|coda]].

mainIdeas.name: The shepherd’s call
mainIdeas.description: a rocking, yodel-like phrase, first in the clarinet, then in the horn, over a drone.

mainIdeas.name: The hymn
mainIdeas.description: a broad, swaying tune in six beats, the shepherds’ song of thanks.

stops.hear: Over a low drone, a clarinet plays a rocking, yodel-like call; a horn answers
The violins sing a broad, swaying hymn tune
stops.happening: The shepherds’ song of thanks, in F major

stops.hear: The tune spreads through the orchestra, to the cellos and then to everyone
A more restless passage, with the tune broken up between instruments
The hymn returns, now broken into rippling quick notes in the violins
The whole orchestra in full voice; the first violins shimmer on a high note
Suddenly very soft and slow, like a prayer

stops.label: Last 30 seconds
stops.hear: A horn plays the shepherd’s call softly one last time; two firm chords

notice: Compare the shepherd’s call at the start with the horn’s call near the end. The same phrase opens and closes the movement.

threads.title: Feeling, not painting
threads.body: The brook, the birds and the storm are there to hear, but Beethoven’s own note asks us to listen for the mood they leave behind.

threads.title: Drones
threads.body: Long held notes run through the symphony: the open chord of the first bars, the village bassoon, the drone under the shepherd’s call. They give it the sound of country music.

threads.title: One continuous ending
threads.body: The dance, the storm and the hymn run together without a break, a single story from fun to fear to thanks.

threads.title: Held-back instruments
threads.body: The timpani and piccolo play only in the storm; the trombones enter in the storm and stay for the hymn.
